# cpanel_addon_domain (Resource)

Manages a cPanel addon domain, its internal subdomain, and document root.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cpanel_addon_domain" "site" {
  domain               = "site.example.net"
  internal_subdomain   = "site-example-net"
  document_root        = "public_html/site"
  delete_document_root = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `document_root` (String) The document root relative to the cPanel account home. cPanel preserves its contents when the addon domain is deleted.
- `domain` (String) The addon domain name.
- `internal_subdomain` (String) The internal subdomain label to create under the cPanel account main domain.

### Optional

- `delete_document_root` (Boolean) Retained for compatibility. The addon domain resource preserves document roots because it cannot prove filesystem ownership; manage owned directory deletion with `cpanel_filesystem_directory`.

### Read-Only

- `domain_key` (String) The cPanel domain key used to identify the addon domain internally.
- `full_subdomain` (String) The complete internal subdomain created for the addon domain.
- `root_domain` (String) The cPanel account main domain that owns the internal subdomain.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cpanel_addon_domain.site site.example.net
```
